data.long_meaning: The name Aran is derived from the Arabic root 'R-N-N', which means 'mountain'. In Islamic context, it symbolizes the firmness and stability of faith. It is also mentioned in the Quran (31:10) as a metaphor for steadfastness. The name Aran carries the meaning “Mountain” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Aran usually hope their child will grow to embody mountain and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun's Muqaddimah, 14th century AD. Aran mentioned as a region in western Iran, inhabited by a people with a distinct cultural identity.
historical_references.context: Ibn Khaldun, a North African historian and sociologist, wrote an influential work known as the Muqaddimah. In it, he described various regions of the Islamic world, including Aran in western Iran. He noted that the people of Aran had a distinct cultural identity and were not Arab, Persian, or Turkish. Aran is believed to correspond to present-day Azerbaijan.

historical_references.reference: Al-Biruni's Al-Athar al-Baqiyah, 11th century AD. Aran mentioned as a region between the Caspian Sea and the Caucasus Mountains, with a predominantly non-Arab population.
historical_references.context: Al-Biruni, an Islamic scholar from Central Asia, wrote an extensive work on the history, geography, and culture of various regions of the Islamic world. In his work Al-Athar al-Baqiyah, he described Aran as a region located between the Caspian Sea and the Caucasus Mountains. He noted that the people of Aran were predominantly non-Arab and had their own distinct cultural identity.
